history.dynasty: None - a folk/devotional shrine of the colonial and post-independence era
history.period: 19th century (believed about 150 years old); present structures built after independence
history.summary: Mahadev Khola Dham is one of the oldest Hindu temples in Meghalaya, a cave temple dedicated to Lord Shiva at Upper Shillong, about 5 km from Shillong bus stand. According to the legend recounted by the temple, the shrine stands where Lakhiya Baba, a sage, chose to meditate; a subedar-major of the 8th Gorkha Regiment dreamt of the sage meditating with a trishul and rudraksha necklace, found him the next day at this spot, and, during excavation for the temple, unearthed a huge shivlinga - hence the Shiva dedication. The earlier temple was built with the permission of the British government; the present temple was built by several persons after independence, in North Indian style, on the banks of the Umshyrpi river. Inside the cave a small opening leads to another cave, and local belief holds it connects directly to the Kamakhya temple atop the Nilachal Hills in Kamrup, Assam (a traditional claim, not an established fact). A small Shiva statue guards the cave entrance, and devotees have added many smaller shrines to the complex. CSV town 'Mairang' is WRONG - the temple is in Shillong (Lawsohtun, Laban, Shillong 793004), roughly 22 km from Mairang; no 'Mahadev Khola Dham' near Mairang itself was found in any source.

name: Mahadev Khola Dham
town: Shillong (Upper Shillong / Laban; CSV town 'Mairang' is incorrect)
town_description: Shillong, the capital of Meghalaya at about 1,525 m in the East Khasi Hills, is the former capital of undivided Assam, known as the 'Scotland of the East'. Its attractions include Shillong Peak, Elephant Falls, Wards Lake, the Don Bosco Museum and a vibrant music culture. Mahadev Khola Dham lies in a verdant gorge at Upper Shillong near Laban (address: Lawsohtun, block 1, Laban, Shillong 793004), about 5 km from Shillong bus stand, on the Shillong Peak route. Mairang, named in the CSV, is a separate town in the Eastern West Khasi Hills about 22 km away; the temple is not there.

travel.airport: Shillong Airport (Umroi) is the nearest airport (verify distance); Guwahati Airport is the nearest major airport (approx. 100-130 km - verify).
travel.railway: Nearest major railway station is Guwahati, Assam (approx. 100-130 km; taxis and buses run to Shillong - verify).
travel.road: About 5 km from Shillong bus stand; 2 km from Shillong city centre near Laban. Reachable by local taxi, auto-rickshaw or private vehicle; vehicles cannot go right up to the shrine - walk about 300 m from the main gate (verify). The temple is on the route to Shillong Peak, about 6 km from the church on that road per Meghalaya Tourism.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Maha Shivaratri (February-March) brings the three-day mela and the largest crowds; quieter visits are best on weekday mornings.
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT between sources: one travel guide lists 6:00 AM to 12:00 PM and 4:30 PM to 6:00 PM; the Meghalaya tourism listing and another guide list 7:00 AM to 7:00 PM daily (verify before visiting). Photography is reported not allowed inside (verify).
